overview: The Climate Equity Council approved past minutes, scheduled their next meeting, and received comprehensive updates on city energy projects, the Electrify Medford campaign, the Hazard Mitigation Plan, and proposed stormwater zoning regulations.

items.title: Administrative Updates and Minutes Approval
items.summary: The council approved the minutes from the October and November meetings and tentatively scheduled their next hybrid meeting for March 19th.

items.title: Medford Connects Events Calendar
items.summary: Members reviewed upcoming local cultural and community events scheduled for February and March, including Black History Month celebrations and International Mother Tongue Day.

items.title: Electrify Medford and Outreach Strategies
items.summary: Brenda Pike reviewed the success of recent direct coaching sessions for heat pumps and sought suggestions for community locations to host future informational sessions.

items.title: City Energy Initiatives and MassSave Policy Changes
items.summary: The council discussed upcoming adjustments to the state's MassSave program rebates and received updates on several municipal projects, including school HVAC installations, a library plug load audit, and a curbside electric vehicle charging grant application.

items.title: Hazard Mitigation Plan Update
items.summary: Brenda Pike outlined the timeline for the five-year update of the city's Hazard Mitigation Plan, which will include public meetings and focus groups through September.

items.title: Zoning Codification and Green Score Proposal
items.summary: The council reviewed a proposed 'Green Score' zoning mechanism designed to incentivize stormwater retention and native plantings in large-scale developments and FEMA flood zones.

items.title: Federal Funding and Community Climate Concerns
items.summary: Members discussed the resilience of local earmarks and tax credits against federal funding freezes, while also noting how federal policy anxieties are impacting outreach within immigrant communities.
